question: Does there exist a public sign-sensitive lift and nonlinear decoder, jointly evaluable below the matched generic square-root baseline, that returns the parity of the canonical generator-relative discrete logarithm?

required_interface.lift_output: a deterministic sign-sensitive, gauge-resolved representation of Q
required_interface.correctness: exact on every canonical scalar representative 0 <= k < ord(G)
required_interface.recovery: bind the exact adaptive parity-to-full-DLP reduction
required_interface.cost: price lift, decoder, precision, preprocessing, memory, exceptions, and all adaptive calls

hard_gates: normalization is computable without the hidden scalar
does not hide an exponential table or a k-step orbit walk
covers zeros, poles, chart changes, extension fields, and exceptional points
beats the matched Pollard-rho baseline in total online work
separates algebraic degree from evaluation complexity
does not infer an algorithm from a coordinate re-encoding alone

closed_mechanism_classes.reason: canonical scalar parity is complemented by point negation
an odd translation cycle cannot support a nonzero order-two character

closed_mechanism_classes.scope: one fixed theta section space with globally linear translation by the full-order generator
closed_mechanism_classes.reason: the line-bundle degree and representation dimension must be at least ord(G)

closed_mechanism_classes.scope: rational functions taking exactly +1 or -1 on every group point
closed_mechanism_classes.reason: the pole degree is at least ceil(ord(G)/2)

surviving_mechanism_classes: finite-field character of a structured rational, division-polynomial, or theta expression
p-adic or analytic theta observable with exact precision and truncation cost
nonlinear cocycle with a global evaluation algorithm that avoids secret-length traversal
high algebraic degree with provably low circuit or recurrence complexity

next_packages.goal: derive a scoped conductor or degree lower bound for exact finite-field-character parity decoders
test division-polynomial, EDS, and theta-multiplication observables that may have high degree but fast evaluation
